title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

deep.reconstruction:
This is the opening page of a note titled 'Sur certains anneaux gradués'. Fix a commutative ring k.

§1. Let M* = ⊕_i M^i be a Z-graded k-module with only finitely many nonzero degrees. Let E* be a subring of End(M*), and let π_i be the canonical projection of M* onto M^i. Assume (1.1) that every π_i lies in E*.

The ring End(M*) carries its usual grading: End^(ν)(M) = ⊕_i Hom(M^i, M^{i+ν}). Equivalently, End^(ν) = Σ_i π_{i+ν} End(M*) π_i, and the degree-ν component of an endomorphism u is pr_ν(u) = Σ_i π_{i+ν} u π_i. Hypothesis (1.1) implies that E* is a graded subring, and that its grading can be described intrinsically from the π_i alone:
- (1.2a) E^(ν) = Σ_i π_{i+ν} E π_i;
- (1.2b) pr_ν^E(u) = Σ_i π_{i+ν} u π_i;
- (1.4) u ∈ E^(ν) ⇔ u π_i = π_{i+ν} u for all i.
The π_i satisfy (relabelled (1.1) in the margin / (1.3) in the text): π_i² = π_i, π_i π_j = 0 for i ≠ j, and Σ π_i = 1.

§2 starts the converse, abstract question. Given an abstract ring E and elements π_i (i ∈ Z), almost all zero, when do these formulas define a ring grading on E? The next page answers: a complete family of orthogonal idempotents suffices. The Peirce decomposition E = ⊕_{i,j} π_j E π_i, regrouped by the difference j − i, gives a grading with E^(ν) E^(ν') ⊂ E^(ν+ν'), and (1.4) holds. In the margin Grothendieck notes that Z could be replaced by any group.

§3 (next page) poses the inverse problem: given a graded ring E*, do such π_i exist, and are they unique, inducing the given grading? Such gradings are 'inner', i.e. induced by an idempotent decomposition.

Purpose, from the title of the dossier: a formal algebra of correspondences for the standard conjectures. Take E = an algebra of (algebraic) correspondences acting on H*(X), and π_i = the Künneth projectors. Standard conjecture C says the π_i are algebraic. That is exactly hypothesis (1.1). Under it, the cohomological grading of the correspondence algebra is intrinsic, i.e. determined by ring-theoretic data. The page builds the purely algebraic scaffolding (later 'Poincaré–Hodge algebras') for that situation.
errors: No mathematical error. Equation numbering is inconsistent. The orthogonal-idempotent relations are labelled (1.3) in the body text but '(1.1)' in the circled marginal insertion, while the membership condition π_i ∈ E* is also (1.1). The next page refers to the idempotent relations as (1.1) and to the grading formulas as (1.2)/(1.3). This is ordinary draft renumbering.

Minor point: finiteness of the grading (or of the support of the π_i) is needed for Σ π_i = 1 and for pr_ν to be a finite sum. Grothendieck does impose it ('à gradation finie', 'nuls sauf un nb fini').
For the uniqueness question begun in §3, uniqueness can only hold up to a shift π_i ↦ π_{i+c}, and up to decomposition into blocks if E is not 'connected'. This is not yet addressed on this page.

ideas.what: A Z-grading on a ring induced by a finite complete family of orthogonal idempotents π_i, via E^(ν) = Σ_i π_{i+ν} E π_i (Peirce decomposition regrouped by degree difference).
ideas.modern_name: Peirce decomposition / 'inner' grading induced by orthogonal idempotents (generalized matrix ring grading)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Peirce; standard in graded ring theory, e.g. Năstăsescu–Van Oystaeyen)
ideas.where_published: Standard conjectures written up in Grothendieck 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (Bombay 1968) and Kleiman's expositions; this specific algebraic formalism is not published as such to my knowledge

ideas.what: Characterization u ∈ E^(ν) ⇔ u π_i = π_{i+ν} u for all i.
ideas.modern_name: Homogeneous elements as intertwiners of the idempotent decomposition

ideas.what: Implicit application: the grading of the algebra of correspondences on H*(X) is intrinsically defined iff the Künneth projectors lie in the algebra (standard conjecture C).
ideas.modern_name: Künneth standard conjecture C; Künneth decomposition of motives (Chow–Künneth decomposition, Murre)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (1969); Kleiman 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures' (Dix exposés)

ideas.what: Converse problem: existence and uniqueness of idempotents inducing a given grading on a graded ring.
ideas.modern_name: Inner gradings / recognising a graded ring as an endomorphism ring of a graded object

missed.claim: This page is the elementary algebraic preamble of Grothendieck's unpublished 'Poincaré–Hodge algebra' formalism. The material on this page itself is classical (Peirce decomposition). Its interest is documentary: it shows Grothendieck reducing the intrinsic definability of the cohomological grading on correspondence algebras to the presence of the Künneth idempotents. That is a ring-theoretic reformulation of conjecture C.
missed.quote: La graduation de E* est définie, intrinsèquement, en termes de la donnée des π_i
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It documents the axiomatic approach to the standard conjectures that Grothendieck pursued in 1966–67. Later work (e.g. Kleiman, André, Kahn on algebras of correspondences and Künneth projectors) covers similar ground, so no new result appears here.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine algebra (complete orthogonal idempotents induce a grading) serving as setup for the correspondence-algebra formalism. It is historically informative but contains nothing new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Top right marginal insertions read roughly 'par Z)' and 'finie' (i.e. 'à gradation (par Z) finie'). The phrase transcribed as 'des modules et graduations[?]' is more likely 'des modules sous-jacents gradués' (uncertain).
The circled block of idempotent relations at the bottom is labelled '(1.1)' in the image, with 'Notons' struck out. The text label '(1.3)' reflects renumbering.
Above 'Soit E* une anneau gradué' the insertion is 'anneau' replacing struck 'k-algèbre'. The interlinear note reads 'nuls sauf un nb fini'.
In §1 the struck phrase before 'pr_ν(u)' is illegible scribble. The superscript 'End^(ν)(M)' is written with parentheses.
The '1' in the top right is the manuscript's own page number; the '2' at bottom left is the archive page number.
